reasons: internal/manifest/manifest_test.go:258 neither new test covers a declaration split across lines, so the regression above is not caught; the added cases only exercise single-line shapes.
notes: The two new tests do genuinely verify the change: with main's manifest.go restored they fail (`org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core was not read` and `an interpolated version must be left empty`). `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass on HEAD.

internal/manifest/manifest.go:282-283 the map branch collects `group|name|version` from the whole line into a map where the last occurrence wins, so a same-line trailing exclusion (`implementation group: 'g', name: 'a', version: '1', { exclude group: 'z', name: 'w' }`) would record `z:w` instead of `g:a`. Rare shape and not a regression (the old parser dropped such lines entirely), but the code comment claims requiring both keys handles this case, which it only does when the exclusion is the sole map on the line.

Suffix matching of configuration names is broader than the old enumeration, but probing a realistic Android/Groovy and Kotlin-DSL build script produced no false positives: non-dependency lines ending in a base name (`openApi { ... }`, `compileOptions`, `maven { url '...' }`) yield no coordinate and are dropped. `classpath` in buildscript and legacy `provided` remain unread, same as before.

Widening the parser increases the chance of two rows with the same (ecosystem,name,version,manifest_path) from one file (e.g. debug/release variants of the same coordinate). internal/indexer/indexer.go:630 inserts these in one multi-row `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, which Postgres rejects with 'cannot affect row a second time'. This is pre-existing (old parser could already emit implementation + testImplementation of the same coordinate) so it is not a reason to block this PR, but it is now easier to hit.
Scope only, no migrations, no auth/secret/workflow changes; the change is a pure code+test change in one package and reverts cleanly.
